title: Too Close To A Holy God

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: When you heard the voice out of the darkness, while the mountain was ablaze with fire, all the leaders of your tribes and your elders came to me. And you said, "The Lord our God has shown us his glory and his majesty, and we have heard his voice from the fire. Today we have seen that a person can live even if God speaks with them. But now, why should we die? This great fire will consume us, and we will die if we hear the voice of the Lord our God any longer." - Deut 5:23-25 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The people were overwhelmed. God's glory blazed on the mountain, His voice thundered from the fire, and they were terrified. "Why should we die?" they cried. They had glimpsed the majesty and holiness of God, and it was more than sinful hearts could bear. Standing near such purity, they felt their own smallness and unworthiness acutely.

This is a healthy fear — the beginning of wisdom (Prov 9:10). We live in a casual age that has largely lost any sense of the awe of God. We speak of Him lightly, approach Him carelessly, forget that He is holy beyond our imagining. The trembling of Israel reminds us that God is not our buddy to be handled casually, but the Holy One before whom angels cover their faces.

And yet — here is the wonder of the gospel — the same holy God has made a way for us to draw near without being consumed. The fire that made Israel tremble was answered at the cross, where Jesus bore the judgment our sin deserved. Now we can "approach God's throne of grace with confidence" (Heb 4:16), not because God became less holy, but because Christ made us clean. Let both truths hold your heart: reverent awe at His holiness, and joyful confidence through His Son.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- Have I lost a healthy sense of awe before God's holiness?
- How do I hold together reverence for God and confidence to approach Him?
- What does it cost God to let me draw near safely?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Holy Lord, You are majestic beyond my understanding, and I bow before You in awe. Thank You that through Jesus I can draw near without fear. Restore in me both reverence and confident joy in Your presence. Amen.
